blockers: E2E data residency confirmation for EU customers
notes: Account snapshot: Sterling Loop builds an in-app product assistant + contextual recommendations for a B2B product analytics suite. Mid-market, global customers with strong EU footprint. Started with Hosted API; pref for move to Dedicated for performance and data isolation.

Initial engagement (Nov 2025): inbound trial via docs + API keys. AE (Maya) ran quick demo focused on streaming chat and embeddings. SE (Diego) did two technical calls on prefix caching and KV cache behavior.

Hosted POC (Jan 2026): 3-week trial using hosted_api. Goals: 95th latency < 250ms for short prompts (<=256 tokens), 99% availability, embeddings similarity > 0.82 on internal benchmark. POC summary: latency median 120ms, 95th 210ms, embeddings mean sim 0.84. Cost estimate from hosted usage: ~20k/mo at current volume.

Decision pivot: want Dedicated to control unit economics at scale and to meet EU data residency + corporate compliance. Key asks: VPC peering, KMS integration, retention controls, audit logs (90 days), SSO (SAML), SOC2 attestation copy.

Dedicated demo (Feb 2026): Diego led walkthrough of Dedicated topology, burst pool mechanics, and autoscale. Sterling product team asked for commit model that supports ramp from 0.5x to 3x of baseline within 30 days without renegotiation.

Pricing/packaging discussion notes: Sterling seeks three-tier commit schedule: initial ramp (month 1-3) at 50% of baseline commit, steady-state commit months 4-12, and 12+ optional uplift. Specific asks: burst pool covering 25% of peak TPS with predictable throttling rules; overage pricing capped at 1.8x committed unit rate; credit for unused committed units quarterly.

Negotiation log: Redwood proposed Dedicated starter commit = $6k/mo equivalent compute credit (expected throughput ~120k tokens/day). Sterling counters with target ARR 100k and wants first-year ramp discount (month 1-3 at 50% invoice). Discussed annual vs monthly billing — Sterling prefers annual commit for price certainty if we provide ramp flexibility and partial credit for unused commit.

Technical risk items flagged: need KMS proof-of-concept to ensure key wrapping works with Dedicated runtime (SEC-1107 ticket opened). Networking: VPC peering across NA and EU regions; ask for private link options. Onboarding: they want an onboarding runbook and SLOs for canary rollouts.

Legal/compliance: legal requested redlines against standard MSA (sent 2026-03-02). NDA done but MSA redline includes data residency and indemnity language for EU customers — blocking signature until resolved.

Commercial concession ask: Sterling asked for a 6-month no-penalty ramp where they can scale commit up or down within 25% without overage charges; Redwood suggested a quarterly true-up and a defined burst allowance. AE documented tradeoffs: lower per-unit price tied to 12-month annual commit + small onboarding credit.

Open items for sales/SE: 1) finalize commit units -> translate to tokens/day and GPU-hour equivalence; 2) define exact burst pool behavior and throttling policy in contract; 3) confirm KMS/HSM integration steps and timeline; 4) produce EU data residency attestation and certs.
Stated customer quote (product lead): 'We need predictable economics for Q3 commercial launch—can't be surprised by token bills. If you give a clear ramp and a fixed burst allowance, we can commit.'

Next steps (detailed): legal to receive final pricing term sheet by 2026-03-12; Diego to run KMS PoC with engineering by 2026-03-18; Maya to schedule procurement/finance call week of 2026-03-22 to finalize billing cadence and ramp schedule; CSM (Rachel) to prepare onboarding timeline draft once contract signed.

Short-term blocker summary: MSA redlines + KMS PoC + confirmation on EU residency certs. Sales plan: present two alternative commercial structures by 2026-03-12 — (A) 12-month annual commit with ramp allowance + credit for unused units; (B) 6-month pilot commit with higher per-unit price and explicit burst pool limits.

Internal notes to Redwood team: prioritize clear mapping from committed $ -> token and GPU-hour equivalence; prepare a sample monthly invoice simulation for Sterling's projected traffic (attach to drive doc). Keep negotiation cadence tight (weekly check-ins).
